From 9569ff1a188fe48b46eb1ac2ae4543c271e0d4c2 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Dan Carpenter <dan.carpenter@oracle.com>
Date: Fri, 24 Jun 2022 09:39:24 +0300
Subject: [PATCH] drm/i915: Fix error code in icl_compute_combo_phy_dpll()
MIME-Version: 1.0
Content-Type: text/plain; charset=UTF-8
Content-Transfer-Encoding: 8bit

This function is supposed to return zero or negative error codes but it
accidentally returns true on failure.

Fixes: 92a020747d6c ("drm/i915: Split shared dpll .get_dplls() into compute and get phases")
Signed-off-by: Dan Carpenter <dan.carpenter@oracle.com>
Signed-off-by: Ville Syrjälä <ville.syrjala@linux.intel.com>
Link: https://patchwork.freedesktop.org/patch/msgid/YrVcHArNMTGCSy+9@kili
Reviewed-by: José Roberto de Souza <jose.souza@intel.com>

diff --git a/drivers/gpu/drm/i915/display/intel_dpll_mgr.c b/drivers/gpu/drm/i915/display/intel_dpll_mgr.c
index ddae7e42ac46..118598c9a809 100644
--- a/drivers/gpu/drm/i915/display/intel_dpll_mgr.c
+++ b/drivers/gpu/drm/i915/display/intel_dpll_mgr.c
@@ -3184,7 +3184,7 @@ static int icl_compute_combo_phy_dpll(struct intel_atomic_state *state,
 	struct icl_port_dpll *port_dpll =
 		&crtc_state->icl_port_dplls[ICL_PORT_DPLL_DEFAULT];
 	struct skl_wrpll_params pll_params = {};
-	bool ret;
+	int ret;
 
 	if (intel_crtc_has_type(crtc_state, INTEL_OUTPUT_HDMI) ||
 	    intel_crtc_has_type(crtc_state, INTEL_OUTPUT_DSI))
-- 
2.25.1

### Modifications in Each File

1. **File: `drivers/gpu/drm/i915/display/intel_dpll_mgr.c`**
   - Changed the type of the variable `ret` from `bool` to `int`. This modification ensures that the function can return negative error codes, as intended, instead of a boolean value which could incorrectly indicate success.

### Relationships Between Modifications

The modification in `intel_dpll_mgr.c` directly addresses a bug in the `icl_compute_combo_phy_dpll()` function. The original implementation mistakenly allowed the function to return a boolean value (true) on failure, which is not appropriate for a function that is expected to return error codes. By changing the variable type to `int`, the function can now correctly return zero or negative values, aligning with its intended behavior and fixing the bug introduced in a previous commit (92a020747d6c). This change is crucial for proper error handling in the driver.

Here is the commit message:
drm/i915: Fix error code in icl_compute_combo_phy_dpll()
MIME-Version: 1.0
Content-Type: text/plain; charset=UTF-8
Content-Transfer-Encoding: 8bit

This function is supposed to return zero or negative error codes but it
accidentally returns true on failure.

Fixes: 92a020747d6c ("drm/i915: Split shared dpll .get_dplls() into compute and get phases")
Signed-off-by: Dan Carpenter <dan.carpenter@oracle.com>
Signed-off-by: Ville Syrjälä <ville.syrjala@linux.intel.com>
Link: https://patchwork.freedesktop.org/patch/msgid/YrVcHArNMTGCSy+9@kili
Reviewed-by: José Roberto de Souza <jose.souza@intel.com>

Here is the root cause:
The bug was caused by the `icl_compute_combo_phy_dpll()` function returning a boolean value (true) on failure instead of the expected zero or negative error codes. This incorrect return type could lead to improper error handling and misinterpretation of the function's success or failure status, as the function was designed to indicate errors through integer return values.

Here is the patch:
 
 static int icl_compute_combo_phy_dpll(struct intel_atomic_state *state,
 				      struct intel_crtc *crtc)
 {
 	struct drm_i915_private *dev_priv = to_i915(crtc->base.dev);
 	struct intel_crtc_state *crtc_state =
 		intel_atomic_get_new_crtc_state(state, crtc);
 	struct icl_port_dpll *port_dpll =
 		&crtc_state->icl_port_dplls[ICL_PORT_DPLL_DEFAULT];
 	struct skl_wrpll_params pll_params = {};
-	bool ret;
+	int ret;
 
 	if (intel_crtc_has_type(crtc_state, INTEL_OUTPUT_HDMI) ||
 	    intel_crtc_has_type(crtc_state, INTEL_OUTPUT_DSI))
 		ret = icl_calc_wrpll(crtc_state, &pll_params);
 	else
 		ret = icl_calc_dp_combo_pll(crtc_state, &pll_params);
 
 	if (ret)
 		return ret;
 
 	icl_calc_dpll_state(dev_priv, &pll_params, &port_dpll->hw_state);
 
 	return 0;
 }
